original_question: Let F be a foliation in Bd with d ≥ 2 that admits a non-zero positive closed current directed by F. What is the resulting function theory of its leaves, especially in terms of the existence and behavior of Green functions?
target_in_paper: Problem 6.1(ii) in §6, “Function theory on foliations by Riemann surfaces,” read together with the definition of B_d given in §4 before Problem 4.1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right target almost exactly: it uses the hypotheses F ∈ B_d with d ≥ 2 and the existence of a nonzero positive closed current directed by F, and it asks about the leafwise function theory through Green functions. It also correctly points to the general part (ii), not the more restrictive part (i). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
missing_details: B_d is not defined in the draft. In the paper, B_d denotes the space of holomorphic foliations on ℙ^2 given in an affine chart ℂ^2 by a polynomial vector field P(z,w)∂/∂z + Q(z,w)∂/∂w with max(deg P, deg Q) = d; this affine notion of degree is the one relevant here. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

The ambient space should be stated explicitly: the question is about foliations on the complex projective plane ℙ^2, described in an affine chart ℂ^2 ⊂ ℙ^2, not about an abstract foliation on an unspecified manifold. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

The current should be identified more precisely as a nonzero positive closed current of bidimension (1,1), directed by (equivalently, tangent to) the foliation. The introduction is where the paper fixes this directed-current language. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

The leaves under discussion are leaves of the foliation on the nonsingular locus, i.e. Riemann-surface leaves away from Sing(F). That is implicit in the paper’s setup and should be made explicit in a stand-alone question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

The nearby context in §6 shows that the Green-function issue is tied to parabolicity: the paper recalls that a Riemann surface is parabolic if all bounded subharmonic functions on it are constant, and uses this to motivate the problem. Mentioning parabolic versus Green-function behavior makes the question sharper and more faithful. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))

The draft should avoid importing the extra assumptions from Problem 6.1(i) (line at infinity invariant; only hyperbolic singularities; excluding compact curves), because those are not part of the official formulation in 6.1(ii). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
refined_question: Let F ∈ B_d with d ≥ 2, where B_d denotes the space of holomorphic foliations on ℙ^2 that, in an affine chart ℂ^2 ⊂ ℙ^2 with coordinates (z,w), are defined by a polynomial vector field P(z,w)∂/∂z + Q(z,w)∂/∂w satisfying max(deg P, deg Q) = d. Assume that F admits a nonzero positive closed current of bidimension (1,1) directed by F. What is the function theory of the leaves of F outside Sing(F), in terms of Green functions; in particular, which leaves are parabolic and which admit Green functions? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
justification: The draft is aiming at Problem 6.1(ii) and not at a neighboring question: its hypotheses match the official statement almost verbatim (F ∈ B_d, d ≥ 2, nonzero positive closed current directed by F, and the focus on Green functions). The surrounding §6 context explains why the sharp stand-alone reformulation should mention leafwise parabolicity together with Green functions: the paper recalls that parabolic leaves force the existence of a directed positive closed current, and contrasts this with Brunella’s no-current situation, where leaves are not parabolic and hence admit Green functions. Section 4 must also be consulted because B_d is defined there, not in §6. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1807.05640))
